text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.89% today to $136.19, recovering modestly from a sharp drop two days earlier. The stock bounced back as oil prices stabilized—US crude holding at $89.53 per barrel and global crude at $92.94—after geopolitical tension in the Middle East had rattled energy markets. Last Monday's 3.8% plunge followed reports of Iranian attacks on US installations in the Gulf, which raised concerns about potential disruptions to oil supply routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

The underlying picture for energy companies remains mixed. While the IEA warned that the Iran conflict has damaged confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable corridor, potential tailwinds are building: a Senate permitting reform bill just passed that could speed up energy projects, and long-term electricity demand is expected to surge as data centers expand to support AI growth. These competing forces—geopolitical risk pulling prices down, but structural demand and policy support pointing upward—explain why ConocoPhillips has been volatile over the past week rather than trending decisively in either direction.
